stemMarkdown: Calculate the volume of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$, in $\text{dm}^3$ at STP ($273.15\text{ K}, 100\text{ kPa}$), produced when $2.50\text{ g}$ of calcium carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$, $M = 100.09\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) reacts completely with excess hydrochloric acid.
stimulusMarkdown: Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP ($273.15\text{ K}, 100\text{ kPa}$) $= 22.7\text{ dm}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

markschemePoints.requirement: Amount of $\text{CaCO}_3$: $n = \frac{2.50}{100.09} = 0.02498\text{ mol}$ ($0.0250\text{ mol}$ to 3 s.f.)
1:1 stoichiometric mole ratio between $\text{CaCO}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$, so $n(\text{CO}_2) = 0.02498\text{ mol}$
Volume $V = 0.02498 \times 22.7 = 0.567\text{ dm}^3$ (to 3 significant figures with correct units)

walkthroughSteps.title: Convert mass of CaCO3 to moles
walkthroughSteps.explanationMarkdown: Divide the given mass by the molar mass: $n = \frac{m}{M} = \frac{2.50}{100.09} = 0.02498\text{ mol}$.

walkthroughSteps.title: Apply molar volume at IB STP (22.7 dm3 mol-1)
walkthroughSteps.explanationMarkdown: Multiply moles of $\text{CO}_2$ by the 2025 IB Data Booklet molar gas volume ($22.7\text{ dm}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$, not $22.4$): $V = 0.02498 \times 22.7 = 0.567\text{ dm}^3$.

commonPitfalls: Using the legacy 22.4 dm3 mol-1 constant instead of the IB Data Booklet value 22.7 dm3 mol-1 at 100 kPa.
Forgetting to round the final answer to 3 significant figures to match 2.50 g.
